alignments.note: Construct noun of the superscription chain; the indefinite *A* belongs to the nominal expression it determines under rule 15, since Hebrew has no indefinite article.

Article on the nomen rectum. The ASV writes no *the* anywhere in the phrase (*A Song of Ascents*), so under rule 29's closing sentence the article is unrepresented; the *A* is the construct noun's own under rule 15 and is not a fronted determiner.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.
Presentative particle rendered *Behold*.

Imperative with its subject pronoun. Rule 36: a *ye* written immediately after the imperative is that verb's subject pronoun, while the second *ye* (t010) stands before the vocative noun and is that noun's.
Definite direct-object marker; the ASV writes the object bare (*bless ye Jehovah*), so rule 16's default applies.
Divine name as object of the imperative.
Quantifier on the vocative phrase, rendered *all*.
Vocative noun with the supplied *ye* standing before it, which rule 36 keeps in the noun's own unit; it is never `added`. Head on the noun carrying the lexeme.
Nomen rectum of `עַבְדֵי יְהוָה`, taking the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Attributive article on the participle, rendered by a relative rather than a *the*; rule 41 gives that relative to the article and heads the unit on it.

Participle keeps its own English verb; the relative before it is the article's under rule 41. Unit discontinuous from its relative only in the sense that the ASV fronts the adverbial phrase *by night* between them (rule 25).
Locative preposition rendered *in*.
Construct noun; no article morpheme stands on it, so the written *the* is supplied to the construct under rule 29, the rectum's own article being absent here.
Nomen rectum taking the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Temporal preposition rendered *by* in *by night*; the phrase is fronted before the participle, so this unit and s018 stand apart from the verb under rule 25.
Article assimilated into the pointed preposition and supplied by MACULA as its own token (rule 12). The ASV writes *by night* with no *the*, so it is unrepresented.
Plural noun rendered by the English singular *night*; the ASV's number is followed as written.

review_notes: The superscription is aligned as ordinary source text: `שִׁיר` takes *A Song* with the indefinite article under rule 15, and the article on `מַעֲלוֹת` is unrepresented because the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all (rule 29).
The verse writes two supplied/written *ye*s; they are allocated by position under rule 36 — the first to the imperative, the second to the vocative `עַבְדֵי`.
`הָעֹמְדִים` is split under rule 41: the article takes the relative *That* and the participle keeps *stand*, with the fronted `בַּלֵּילוֹת` standing between them (rule 25).

alignments.note: Imperative rendered by an English phrasal verb; *up* is the verb's own particle under rule 44 and the head stays on the lexical verb.
Construct dual noun rendered *hands*; the possessive standing before it is the suffix's under rule 18, so the unit is discontinuous in English order only.
Pronominal suffix realized by the possessive *your* (rule 18).

Bare nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it; the supplied *to* states what the nominal contributes and belongs to it under rule 33, and the supplied *the* determines the nominal expression under rule 15. Head on the word carrying the lexeme. The ASV margin offers *Or, in holiness*, which is read and set aside under rule 38: the printed text governs.
Conjunction rendered *And* (rule 14).
Imperative with its subject pronoun written immediately after the verb (rules 17 and 36); no vocative stands in this clause to compete for it.
Object marker; the ASV writes the object bare, so rule 16's default applies.
Divine name as object of the imperative.

review_notes: `קֹדֶשׁ` stands with no preposition and no marker on it, so both the supplied *to* and the supplied *the* join its unit under rules 33 and 15 rather than being marked `added`.
The marginal alternative *Or, in holiness* was read and set aside under rule 38; the printed *to the sanctuary* is what is aligned.

alignments.note: Jussive verb rendered *bless*; the ASV fronts the subject name before it, so the unit stands after t001 under rule 25.
Object suffix realized by *thee* (rule 18).
Explicit subject noun taking only its own English word (rule 20).
Ablative `מִן` rendered by the multi-word preposition *out of*, headed on the token carrying the lexeme under rule 24.
Place name.

Anarthrous participle used substantivally; no article morpheme is present, so the supplied *he that* joins the participle's own unit under rule 46 and the head goes to the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31). The competing reading would head on *he*, but rule 46 expressly ranks the substantive's own lexeme above a pronoun the ASV supplied.

Appositional *Even* standing before a phrase no object marker and no connective morpheme reaches. The clause writes no waw and no `אֵת` here, so under rule 16's limit and rule 14's closing sentences no morpheme licenses the word and it is its own `added` unit; it is not folded into the participle's unit standing beside it (rule 42's reasoning about a surplus *and*).
Object of the participle.
Conjunction rendered *and* (rule 14).
Second coordinated object.

review_notes: `עֹשֵׂה` is an anarthrous substantival participle, so its supplied *he that* joins its own unit under rule 46 and is not `added`; the head is *made*, not the supplied pronoun.
*Even* is marked `added`: the verse writes no object marker for it to stand on and no connective morpheme in that colon, so neither rule 16's appositional *even* nor rule 14's connective reaches it.
